description: Declarative list of prjxray-db files this repo freezes into data/, plus the bit-class taxonomy those files are cut into. The extractor (scripts/extract_prjxray_subset.py) reads this file; it is the only place the subset is defined.

source.name: prjxray-db
source.note: Upstream is archived. Freezing the static .db/.json text fully resolves the dependency; the fuzzers that produced it are NOT a dependency and are never resurrected (docs/kickoff_fuzz_and_map.md §4).

cross_family_reference.claim: 7-series shares one fabric: prjxray's zynq7 rule files are byte-identical to artix7. Groups with cross_family_check=true are re-verified at every extraction, so the 2026-07-11 audit is a machine-checked fact in the manifest, not a remembered one.

groups.rationale: INT switchbox PIP rules. The routing-class inventory; certified host-side now, exercised on silicon only on sacrificial hardware (kickoff §1 electrical layer).
Pseudo-PIPs in INT tiles: connections with no configuration bits (always/default). Needed so the gate does not go looking for bits that cannot exist.
INT_INTERFACE tiles bridge CLB pins to the INT switchbox and are entirely pseudo-PIP (no segbits file upstream). Required to walk a route from a slice pin into the switchbox.

CLB configuration bits: LUT INIT, LUTRAM/SRL mode, FF config, and the slice-local output/carry muxes. This is the class evolution consumes today (worst case of a wrong write is logic garbage, never contention).
Bit-less connections inside CLB tiles; same purpose as int_ppips.
Per-tile-type bit masks. A specimen diff hits bits that belong to no documented feature; the mask says which of those are known-uninteresting, so an uncertified-bit alarm means something.

Device-specific, not fabric rules: which tile sits where on this die, which frame address and bit offset a tile's bits live at, and how tiles' wires connect. Maps a feature name to an actual bit in an actual bitstream.
Our exact part. required_features.fasm is what any generated bitstream must carry to be loadable.
part -> device -> fabric resolution, and the element census used as a sanity check on tilegrid parsing.
Upstream licence (CC0-1.0) and README, frozen alongside the data so the vendoring is self-documenting.

bit_classes.rationale: LUT truth-table bits. Silicon-proven across the whole zynq-ehw / zynq-xpart / zynq-autoehw line; certified first because M2 consumes it immediately.
bit_classes.board_safety: content — a wrong write is a logic error, not a short

bit_classes.rationale: SLICEM distributed-RAM / SRL mode selects. Changes what the LUT bits mean, so it must be certified before LUT-INIT edits are trusted inside a SLICEM.
Flip-flop init/reset/clock-enable configuration. Content-class and directly useful as extra genome real estate.

Slice-local selects (FF input, slice output, carry init). Fan-in selectors, so an invalid encoding is a bad select rather than a driver conflict — but they are the first class where the one-selected-input-per-mux-group rule of the safety_whitelist actually bites.
Switchbox PIPs. Host-side certification is free and builds inventory; on-silicon routing evolution waits for sacrificial hardware (kickoff §1).
bit_classes.board_safety: routing — contention-capable, NEVER autonomously fuzzed on a working EBAZ

bit_classes.rationale: Bit-less pseudo-PIPs across INT, INT_INTERFACE and CLB tiles. Certification is a negative assertion: a specimen that routes through one of these must produce an empty frame diff.

notes: IOB/IOI, BRAM, DSP, CLK and HCLK tile classes are deliberately NOT frozen in v1.0.0: nothing in this line touches them, and a subset whose every line is classified is what makes the unclassified_policy=fail invariant meaningful. Adding a group is a MINOR spec bump plus a re-extraction.
mask_int_*.db does not exist upstream (INT tiles have no mask file); this is expected, not a missing file.
Certification status does not live here. This spec says what is frozen and how it is cut into classes; the prediction gate writes certificates, and MANIFEST.json carries the current status per class.
